paper_metadata.title: Experimental investigation of a Portevin-Le Chatelier band in Ni-Co-based superalloys in relation to gamma' precipitates at 500 ℃

evidence.section: Abstract
evidence.quote: The macroscopically localized deformation behaviors of Ni–Co-based superalloys with different precipitates content were investigated at 500 C and 1×10 −4 s−1 via an in situ method namely, digital image correlation (DIC).

evidence.section: 2. Materials and experimental procedure
evidence.quote: Two nickel‒cobalt-based superalloys designed with various precipitates volume fractions (5% and 30%) were considered in this work.

evidence.section: 1. Introduction
evidence.quote: the microscopic origin of the PLC effect is attributed to the dynamic interactions between the mobile dislocations and the diffusing solutes, i.e., the dynamic strain aging (DSA).

evidence.section: 3.3. Localized deformation bands associated with precipitates
evidence.quote: the effective aging time for solute diffusion to the temporarily arrested dislocations increases, which leads to a significant interaction during the DSA process and consequently large magnitude serrations.

evidence.section: 3.2. Stress–strain curves and the corresponding serration amplitudes
evidence.quote: The yield strength and the ultimate strength of the 30% alloy are considerably greater than those of the 5% alloy due to the second-phase strengthening effect.

evidence.section: 3.1. Microstructures observed via OM and TEM
evidence.quote: It can be speculated that the SF density of the 30% alloy was also much higher than that of the 5% alloy at lower strain rate of 1×10 -4 s-1.

evidence.section: 3.3. Localized deformation bands associated with precipitates
evidence.quote: numerous interactions between SFs and Suzuki segregation can also retard dislocation motion and subsequently introduce DSA effects.
